2607.16112.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
2607.16112.paper_summary: Frontier AI companies have published capability thresholds that differ substantially, making it difficult for third parties to verify whether a threshold has been crossed or to compare requirements across companies. Moreover, without common minimum thresholds, risk mitigation may be inconsistent, creating a potential race to the bottom in safety standards. We develop a methodology for deriving harmonized thresholds across three risk domains. For misuse risks (cyber and biological), we take expected harm as the key primitive and use an explicit risk-modeling approach that accounts for risk channels and model release conditions. For automated AI R&D, we base our proposed threshold on the observed rate of AI progress rather than expected harm. Our analysis expands upon prior work and highlights existing empirical gaps and limitations.
2607.16112.paper_summary_zh: 前沿的人工智慧公司已發布的能力門檻差異顯著，使第三方難以驗證是否已超過某一門檻或在公司之間比較要求。此外，若沒有共同的最低門檻，風險緩解可能不一致，這可能導致安全標準的潛在競爭下降。我們開發了一種方法論，以在三個風險領域中推導出統一的門檻。對於誤用風險（網絡和生物），我們將預期傷害視為關鍵原始概念，並使用明確的風險建模方法，考慮風險通道和模型發布條件。對於自動化的人工智慧研發，我們所提出的門檻基於人工智慧進展的觀察速率，而非預期傷害。我們的分析擴展了先前的研究，並突顯了現有的實證空白和限制。
